title: A Tiny Fish Passed the Mirror Test, Like Chimps and Dolphins

scenes.text: Few animals recognize themselves in a mirror. One's a fish.
scenes.keywords: fish looking at mirror underwater coral

scenes.text: Scientists put a colored mark on a cleaner wrasse where it could only see it in a mirror.
scenes.keywords: small colorful fish coral reef close up

scenes.text: The fish looked in the mirror, then scraped its body on rocks to rub the mark off.
It ignored clear marks. And it ignored colored marks when there was no mirror.
That's the same kind of test chimpanzees and dolphins are famous for passing.
A fish looked in a mirror and figured out one thing: that's me.

description:
Few animals recognize themselves in a mirror. One of them is a fish.
In a 2019 PLOS Biology study, cleaner wrasses scraped at a mark they could only see in a mirror, but not at clear marks or when no mirror was present.
Do you think a fish can be self-aware? Comment below.
thumbnail_text: A FISH PASSED THE MIRROR TEST
first_comment: Chimps and dolphins pass this test. Did you expect a fish to join them?
